question.leadin: As much as 70% of the male population of this country may have been killed in the disastrous War of the Triple Alliance.
question.text: Name this country which was led by Francisco Solano Lopez from 1862 until he was killed in action in 1870.
question.clue: The most vilified leader of this country was a paramour of Eliza Lynch who shouted "I die with my nation!" at the Battle of Cero Cora.

swap.leadin: He met with Jose de San Martin at the Guayaquil Conference.
swap.text: Name this early 19th-century South American leader nicknamed "The Liberator."
swap.clue: This winning commander at Carabobo joined with Antonio Jose de Sucre to win a victory at Ayacucho.

question.leadin: Jean-Jacques Dessalines granted the citizens of this country freedom of religion, which had been denied them by Toussaint L'Ouverture.
question.text: Name this Caribbean country, the second to win independence from a European power after the United States. Rafael Trujillo [tru-he-yo] organized the Parsley Massacre against people from this country in 1937.
question.answerHtml: Republic of Haiti [or Republique d’Haiti; or Ayti; or Repiblik Dayti]
question.clue: A non-monarchial ruler of this country had formerly worked as a coachman, and owned several large plantations.

swap.text: Forces under Antonio Jose de Sucre won this decisive 1824 battle to ensure Peruvian independence. Following this battle, Jose de Canterac signed a capitulation for the Royalist forces.
swap.clue: After San Martin gave his troops to Bolivar, the newly combined forces helped liberate Peru by winning this 1824 battle named for a city in the modern Huamanga Province. This battle's result led to the surrender of the main royalist resistance.

question.leadin: This dictator led his country through the Special Period after the fall of the Soviet Union.
question.text: Name this leader of the 26th of July Revolution, who gave the "History Will Absolve Me" speech after being arrested for leading an attack on the Moncada ("mohn-KAH-dah") Barracks.
question.clue: Che Guevara joined this man's 26th of July Movement.

swap.leadin: After this man took power in 1973, his regime used the country's national stadium as a prison camp and torture facility.
swap.text: Name this dictator who overthrew the Marxist Salvador Allende in a military coup.
swap.clue: On his 60th birthday, the CIA launched Operation Condor to suppress left-wing movements in this man's nation and neighboring Argentina.

question.text: This Mexican port city was taken in early 1847 by an amphibious assault, paving the way for the eventual capture of Mexico City.
question.clue: Admiral Frank Friday Fletcher prevented the S.S. Ypiranga from unloading its cargo in this city to enforce an arms embargo.

swap.text: This Argentine liberator fought in the Peninsular War and was given the title "Protector of Peru." He was the winning commander at Chacabuco and Maipu, and helped liberate Chile from Spanish rule.
swap.clue: This leader defeated Manuel Osorio alongside Bernardo O'Higgins at Maipu after winning at Chacabuco.

question.leadin: Literacy tests in this country meant that most of its Black population was ineligible to vote in postwar elections.
question.text: Name this country where a civil rights agenda was promoted in the 1960s by a politician nicknamed Jango, who served as a vice president under Juscelino Kubitschek ("zhoo-seh-LEE-noo koo-bee-SHEK").
question.answerHtml: Brazil [or Federative Republic of Brazil or República Federativa do Brasil]
question.clue: The Constitutionalist Revolution in this country, which demanded one ruler's power be checked, was also known as the Paulista War which, like the Pernambuco Revolt, was named for one of this country's states.

swap.leadin: Politics in the Caribbean can be a tough business.
swap.text: This strongman led Panama from 1983 to 1989. He was overthrown in a U.S. invasion, transported to Miami, and served seventeen years in prison for drug-related crimes.
swap.clue: After the death of Robert Paz, the U.S. invaded the country of this former CIA informant in Operation Nifty Package.

question.text: Jose Napoleon Duarte presided throughout much of a twelve-year civil war in this Central American country. In this country, the politically active Archbishop Oscar Romero was killed at the altar.
question.answerHtml: Republic of El Salvador [or Republica de El Salvador]
question.clue: The killing of Rutilio Grande in this country prompted liberation theologian, Archbishop Oscar Romero, to refuse to attend state occasions.

swap.text: In 1960, the most powerful earthquake ever recorded hit the city of Valdivia in this seismically-active South American country, which shares the southern Andes with Argentina.
swap.clue: After its neighbor imposed a ten cent tax on this country's saltpeter production, this country seized the city of Antofagasta and triggered a war which landlocked that neighbor.

question.leadin: Bartolome de Las Casas lamented the unnecessary deaths of natives in this system before they were able to understand "the true faith or sacraments."
question.text: Name this system of colonial labor, which Las Casas called a "moral pestilence." This system, akin to slavery, awarded the labor of indigenous peoples to the Spanish colonial elite.
question.clue: Despite the fact that religious orders retained control over all lands under its jurisdiction, reformers like Bartolome de las Casas sought to eliminate all systems under which natives were assimilated.

swap.leadin: President Juan Manuel Santos has begun peace talks with this group after the 2011 death of its leader, Alfonso Cano.
swap.text: Identify this Marxist guerrilla group formed by the PCC in the aftermath of La Violencia that now fights alongside the ELN for control of Colombia.
swap.answerHtml: FARC [or Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia—People’s Army; or Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias de Colombia—Ejército del Pueblo]
swap.clue: Comically evil death squads like CONVIVIR were authorized to fight this group, which effectively controls nearly 200,000 miles of jungle in its home country.

question.leadin: While he was a member of a guerrilla organisation, this politician adopted the name Aureliano in homage to a Colonel in One Hundred Years of Solitude.
question.text: Elected in 2022, this politician is the first leftwing President in his country's history, and his vice-president Francia Marquez is the first black woman to hold the post.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Latin American wars.
swap.text: This 1836-1839 war was sparked when Peru and Bolivia attempted to merge into the single namesake country. It turned when Chile joined the effort after a series of comical misunderstandings and abortive coups turned reviled general Diego Portales into a national martyr.
swap.answerHtml: War of the Confederation [accept: War of the Peru-Bolivian Confederation; Guerra contra la Confederación Perú-Boliviana]
swap.clue: Diego Portales, the powerful defense minister who started this war, was assassinated in its second year, greatly increasing public support for this conflict on the winning side.

question.text: Specific term required. To decry Black suffrage in Jamaica and Trinidad, Froude alleged that Haitians ate babies as part of this Afro-diasporic tradition. The "Saint Lucia horror" was blamed on this healing tradition after the Leeward Islands banned it in 1904.
question.answerHtml: obeah [or obeahism, obi, obia, obayi, obeya, or other variants; accept myal; accept Obeah Act]
question.clue: This type of folk magic of Igbo origin was outlawed in Jamaica after Tacky's War. Queen Nanny was often described as a practitioner of it by contemporary documents.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the War of the Triple Alliance.
swap.text: This battle, won by the Paraguayans, prevented the advance of allied forces for over a year. The Paraguayan failure to counterattack kept the battle from being more than a temporary success.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Argentina's economic woes since the 1970s.
question.text: This was Argentina's currency at the time of Menem's election. Juan Vital Sourrouille ("soo-REEL") introduced this currency in 1985 under a namesake economic plan, but it only lasted until 1991 before being replaced by the convertible peso.

swap.text: This leader of the Generation of 1837, known in Argentina as "The Teacher," wrote a critique on Rosas called Facundo. He later served as Argentina's seventh president.
swap.clue: This Argentine politician, president of Argentina from 1868 to 1874.
